blocks.content: English stress makes one syllable *louder*. Japanese **pitch accent** makes one syllable *higher* in tone. Every word has a pitch pattern, and in some cases the pattern is the only thing distinguishing two otherwise identical words.
The Tokyo dialect (standard Japanese) is the reference system used in textbooks and broadcast media. Pitch is described as H (high) or L (low) per mora.
橋 and 箸 look identical in romaji and share the same kanji sounds : pitch is the *only* distinguishing feature. In a real sentence, context almost always resolves meaning before pitch even matters.

Getting pitch accent wrong does not prevent communication. Native speakers adjust easily for non-native speech. Pitch is best absorbed through listening : it improves naturally with exposure and can be studied deliberately at intermediate level. For now, focus on vocabulary, grammar, and reading.
